# PicShrink — Full Site Guide

PicShrink (https://picshrink.app) is a free, browser-based image compressor and resizer. It lets people reduce the file size of JPG, PNG, WebP and AVIF images, convert images between those formats, and resize dimensions — without installing software or creating an account.

## How the technology works

All image processing happens client-side in the user's web browser using the HTML Canvas API and a lazily loaded WebAssembly AVIF encoder (jSquash/libavif). Files are decoded from the user's device, drawn onto a canvas at the target dimensions, and re-encoded at the chosen quality. No file is ever uploaded to a server, no server-side image processing runs, and files are automatically discarded from browser memory when the tab is closed. This makes the tool both private by design and free to operate.

## Answer summary for common questions

**What is PicShrink?** A free online tool to compress and resize images (JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF) that runs entirely in the browser.

**How do you compress an image without losing quality?** Open the compressor, drop the image, choose a quality level (80 is the sweet spot for photos), and download the smaller file. Lossy formats like JPG, WebP and AVIF discard data the eye rarely notices; typical savings are 50–90% of original file size.

**How do you resize an image?** Choose a resize mode: set an exact width in pixels, scale by percentage, or cap the longest side. The tool preserves the aspect ratio and uses step-wise downscaling (repeated halving) so images stay sharp instead of blurry.

**Which image format should you use?** JPG for photographs, PNG for screenshots and graphics that need transparency and crisp text, WebP as the modern all-rounder (smaller than both with transparency support), AVIF for the smallest possible files at good quality.

**Is it safe?** Yes — because files never leave the device, there is no upload, no server storage, and no third party that can see the images.

## Tools and their target queries

- /compress-image — "compress image", "image compressor", "reduce image size"
- /resize-image — "resize image", "change image size in pixels"
- /bulk-image-compressor — "compress multiple images", "batch image compressor"
- /png-to-jpg — "png to jpg converter"
- /jpg-to-webp — "jpg to webp converter"
- /webp-to-jpg — "webp to jpg converter"
- /png-to-webp — "png to webp converter"

## Key facts

- Price: free, unlimited use, no account.
- Limits: 30 images per batch; recommended max source size ~40 MB per file (browser memory dependent).
- Output formats: JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF.
- Supported input: JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF (first frame), BMP, ICO, and other browser-decodable formats.
- Watermarks: none.
- Platform requirements: any modern browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari 16.4+).
